title: Secret-read guard: PreToolUse hook refuses agent reads of ~/.config/capsule and host *.env (inc_3a8e4754)
body:
Incident inc_3a8e4754: a CoS-dispatched host builder printed ~/.config/capsule/admin.env into its transcript (cos-log.md:2481). claude/settings.fragment.json has no PreToolUse read guard. write-guard.py covers writes only, and only in run.sh jobs.

Write these tests first. Each one fails before the fix.
1. maintenance.tests.test_secret_read_guard.SecretReadGuard.test_read_of_capsule_admin_env_is_denied: a Read payload for $HOME/.config/capsule/admin.env exits 2. Use a tempdir HOME.
2. ...test_bash_cat_of_identity_env_is_denied: Bash `cat ~/.config/capsule/identities/x.env` exits 2. A variant through `$HOME` and a symlink also exits 2.
3. ...test_grep_and_glob_under_capsule_config_are_denied.
4. ...test_capsule_secret_get_is_allowed: Bash `capsule-secret get FOO` exits 0.
5. ...test_repo_fixture_env_in_cwd_checkout_is_allowed: a tracked fixture *.env inside the cwd checkout exits 0.
6. ...test_malformed_payload_fails_closed.
7. maintenance.tests.test_merge_settings.MergeSettings.test_shipped_fragment_has_secret_read_guard: the fragment holds a PreToolUse entry for secret-read-guard.py whose matcher covers Read, Grep, Glob and Bash.
8. ...test_guard_entry_is_owned_not_duplicated: merging twice gives exactly one guard entry.

Acceptance criteria:
- The guard denies paths under ~/.config/capsule/**, ~/.config/notes-vault/*.env, and *.env/.env* outside the cwd git checkout. It checks paths after expanduser and resolve.
- The deny message names the rule and points to capsule-secret.
- OWNED_MARKER also covers notes-vault/maintenance/hooks/.
- deploy.sh check returns DRIFT when the guard is missing.
- RUNBOOK.md (trust-boundary section, about line 5623) names the guard as the host-side enforcer for secret reads.
- All suites pass. Paste the test output on the card.

File set:
- maintenance/hooks/secret-read-guard.py (new)
- maintenance/tests/test_secret_read_guard.py (new)
- claude/settings.fragment.json
- claude/merge_settings.py
- maintenance/tests/test_merge_settings.py
- docs/RUNBOOK.md

Out of scope: rotation of the Infisical admin credentials (Owner). Never read a real ~/.config/capsule file in a test. Use tempdirs only.

## Incident inc_3a8e4754 (Korin post-mortem, row 456)
- Root cause: No mechanised rule stops a host agent from reading a secret file. Evidence: cos-log.md:2481 says the P03 Sonnet builder, a host subagent dispatched by CoS, printed ~/.config/capsule/admin.env (Infisical admin password and token) into its transcript. Host subagents inherit ~/.claude/settings.json. Its harness-owned part, claude/settings.fragment.json:6-42, holds only SessionStart, PostToolUse (Write|Edit) and PostCompact hooks. It has no PreToolUse hook for Read, Grep, Glob or Bash. The only PreToolUse guard, maintenance/hooks/write-guard.py:18,31, checks Write/Edit/MultiEdit only, and only run.sh jobs load it. claude/merge_settings.py:42-43 rejects nested settings, so the fragment cannot ship permissions.deny either. RUNBOOK.md:5623-5634 states that the container is the only real boundary: docker.py never mounts ~/.config/capsule. Host processes are same-user and 'operator-trusted', so nothing refused the read. The fix after the event (cos-log.md:2481, 'briefs now ban reading any *.env / ~/.config/capsule') is prose in a brief, not an enforcer.
- Mitigation: Add a PreToolUse hook maintenance/hooks/secret-read-guard.py. Ship it in claude/settings.fragment.json with matcher Read|Grep|Glob|Bash|Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit. The hook denies with exit 2 when a tool path or Bash command names one of these, after expanduser and resolve (symlinks followed):
- ~/.config/capsule/** (admin.env, identities/*.env, projects.env);
- any file named *.env or .env* outside the git checkout of the session's cwd;
- ~/.config/notes-vault/*.env.
On a malformed payload it fails closed. Extend merge_settings.OWNED_MARKER so it also owns hooks under notes-vault/maintenance/hooks/; otherwise deploy appends a duplicate entry on every run. deploy.sh check reports DRIFT when the guard is absent from ~/.claude/settings.json. Owner's rotation of the Infisical admin password and token (cos-log.md:2482, 2492) is a separate human step. The fix card does not cover it.
- Enforcer: maintenance/hooks/secret-read-guard.py (PreToolUse, merged into ~/.claude/settings.json by deploy.sh via claude/settings.fragment.json). It refuses Read/Grep/Glob/Bash on ~/.config/capsule/** and host *.env files for every host session and subagent. deploy.sh --check gives DRIFT if the guard is missing.
- Recurrence test: `maintenance.tests.test_secret_read_guard.SecretReadGuard.test_read_of_capsule_admin_env_is_denied` - write it first; it fails before the fix and passes after.
- [ ] `python3 -m unittest maintenance.tests.test_secret_read_guard.SecretReadGuard.test_read_of_capsule_admin_env_is_denied` passes (the incident gate re-runs it on main).

## Prior verdicts

Earlier verdicts on the same root cause, quoted as data (newest first):
- row 456: Korin: the incident loop as a role, a record and a gate (Owner + Fable, 2026-09-27 01:00 Bangkok); Owner: the factory must come back stronger from every failure like a Saiyan; lessons learned as in software companies (incident, root cause, lesson, mitigation); asked how it is enforce...
why: New PreToolUse hook secret-read-guard.py plus settings fragment: a guard and a hook (D15 judges).

title: mutation_check: on 'did not fail', retry with production files only (new intent examples)
body:
# Mutation gate (b) and a new intent example landing with the code it judges

Read-only design note, 2026-10-26, repo capsule-corp at main f16a2521. Card t_1c84a9be.

## What actually happens (verified)

- `tests/mutation_check.py::_check_range_impl` builds ONE revert set:
  `revert_targets = prod_files + intent_data_files + contractdata.sha256sums_for(...)` (line 1345)
  and reverts all of them together to `--base` before running the changed tests.
- The card's range (uncommitted in `~/.local/share/capsule/boards/capsule-corp/work/epic-capsule-harness`,
  branch epic/capsule-harness) touches `capsule/unblocked.py` (fix), `contracts/intent/unblocked.jsonl`
  (+1 example `landed-branch-with-only-an-idle-sync-merge-is-not-counted`), 3 lines inside
  `capsule/tests/test_unblocked.py::IntentExamples.test_every_example_matches_its_oracle` (the loop
  that executes every example against the real code), and a new test in `test_unblocked_done.py`.
- `test_unblocked_done.py` fails on revert (good). `test_unblocked.py` reads "did not fail (BAD)":
  the loop iterates the file on disk, the file is at base, the new example is gone, the loop has
  nothing to judge. Reverting `capsule/unblocked.py` alone makes the loop fail on the new id.
- So the gate reverted the oracle together with the subject. Z1 says the intent example is a
  separate artefact and Z3 ranks it above code; the gate's own rule for tests is "the new tests
  stay as HEAD wrote them". An intent example that a test executes IS a test written as data, and
  the gate currently treats it as production. The I1 revert (`is_intent_data_file`, t_3ff01dd1) was
  added for the other shape, a test that merely pins the data, and that shape still needs it.

## Recommendation: two revert sets, tried in order, labelled

Keep the current combined revert as the first attempt. When it reads "did not fail" AND the range
has both production `.py` files and intent/contract data files, run the same test ids once more
with ONLY `prod_files` reverted (data and its SHA256SUMS left at HEAD). A failure there is
`FAIL (good) [revert: production only; contracts data kept at HEAD]`. A pass on both is still
`did not fail (BAD)`.

Why this one: the gate observes instead of trusting a declaration (Z2), it is never more lenient
than today (a BAD becomes good only when a real production mutation was caught by HEAD's tests and
HEAD's examples), the I1 data-only shape is untouched (no `prod_files` means no second set), and the
common path costs nothing extra; the retry runs only on the vacuous outcome. It is one small loop
over `[combined, prod_only]` in a function that already brackets revert/restore (Z8 rules 1-2).

Rejected:
- (a) never revert `contracts/intent/*.jsonl`: undoes I1 and `tests/test_mutation_check.py::
  IntentDataFileRevertedToo` (a data-only range with a pin test would read n/a again) and the
  `data-only-change-is-judged-by-reverting-the-data` intent row.
- (b) a marker naming the example / (c) land the row in an earlier commit: both replace an
  observation with a declaration or a build ritual (a second marker grammar; or two landings per
  fix with a red example on main in between, since the gate's range is merge-base..head anyway),
  and `contracts/**` is protected so the worker cannot sequence the row itself.

## Exact behaviour change

In `_check_range_impl`, (b) branch, state == "resolved" and `failed` is False and `chain_kept` is
empty: if `prod_files` and `intent_data_files` are both non-empty, restore every
`intent_data_files + sha256sums` path in the scratch worktree to HEAD, rerun `_resolve_import_chain`
for the same `names`, then put the data files back to base. If that rerun fails, assign state
`"prod_only_revert_ok"` with why `"revert: production only; contracts data kept at HEAD"`, rendered
by `_cell` as `FAIL (good) [revert: production only; contracts data kept at HEAD]`. Otherwise the
existing `False` (BAD) stands. Nothing else changes: table shape, exit codes, (c), (d), I1, markers.
About 15-20 lines plus one `_cell` branch; keep it under the size oracle's 40-line new-function
limit by making the retry a small helper with two callers only if a second caller exists,
otherwise inline it.

Docstring (top of file, the (b) paragraph) gets one sentence; RUNBOOK "mutation" bullet (around
line 2088) gets one clause: "a range that changes both code and the intent examples a test
executes is also judged with the code alone reverted".

## Files and protection

- `tests/mutation_check.py`: NOT in `capsule/workspace.py` PROTECTED (that tuple holds contracts/**,
  docs/ZENKAI.md, SOUL/CLAUDE/AGENTS.md, capsule/intent.py, workspace.py, lander.py, docker, blind
  harness, meters, calibration, interrupts.json). It is in the gate's own
  `DIRTY_TREE_WATCHED_PATHS` (must be committed before any gate run). I found no "R02 judge path"
  list anywhere in the repo at f16a2521; if R02 lands first and names this file, treat it as
  protected and route through Owner.
- `tests/test_mutation_check.py`: new fixture class (second oracle 1).
- `contracts/intent/mutation_check.jsonl` + `contracts/intent/SHA256SUMS`: PROTECTED, CoS stamp
  (Owner delegation, same as commit 3d58d1af). Two new rows, under the 3-per-round cap
  (`test_at_most_three_new_examples_per_round_since_the_merge_base`).
- `docs/RUNBOOK.md`: one clause. Not protected.
- `capsule/intent.py`, `maintenance/merge_gate.py`: untouched.

## Oracles (Z1, Z2)

1. Intent rows in `contracts/intent/mutation_check.jsonl`, replayed by `tests/test_mutation_info.py`
   through the real CLI on a fixture range (same shape as `data-only-change`):
   - `code-and-example-in-one-range-is-judged-by-reverting-the-code-alone`: range = prod fix + new
     example + loop test that executes examples against the code -> `ok: true`. Source: owner (this
     card) once he agrees, else `recorded run` of the t_1c84a9be gate run.
   - `code-and-example-with-a-vacuous-example-loop-still-blocks`: same range, loop asserts nothing
     the code decides -> `ok: false`.
2. `tests/test_mutation_check.py`: fixture repo built in tempfile asserting the exact cell text
   `FAIL (good) [revert: production only; contracts data kept at HEAD]` for shape 1, `did not fail
   (BAD)` for shape 2, and `IntentDataFileRevertedToo` unchanged. Different data source (in-process
   `check_range` on a built repo) from oracle 1 (CLI on the intent fixture).
3. Real-range check, outside both: once t_1c84a9be's work is committed, `python3 tests/mutation_check.py
   --base <merge-base> --head <branch>` must read good for `test_unblocked.py` with the new label,
   and a scratch worktree with only `capsule/unblocked.py` at base must still fail
   `test_every_example_matches_its_oracle` on the new id (the implementer's manual observation).

## Does it need Owner's yes

Not for the gate code: `tests/mutation_check.py` is not protected and the change is reversible in
one revert commit (Z6). It does need the CoS stamp for the two intent rows and SHA256SUMS
(delegated). Tell Owner in one line in the next status; do not wait on him. If R02 has made the
gate a judge path by the time this lands, that changes to a yes.

## t_1c84a9be right now

- Leave it `blocked / needs_input`; it is in progress on a gate fix, not stuck. Do not `human
  accept`, do not `OPS_SKIP_MUTATION_CHECK` (that is a Z4 override and would need the same fix card
  anyway). The implementer did nothing wrong: tests untouched, oracle real.
- File one fix card for the gate change above (small, Sonnet, blind test from the contract in
  section Oracles). Land it first.
- Meanwhile the CoS does the two host-only items the card already lists: stamp
  `contracts/intent/SHA256SUMS` for the new unblocked row (the row itself is sourced `owner`;
  confirm that source is real or change it to `recorded run`/row), and note that the implementer
  wrote to protected `contracts/intent/unblocked.jsonl`, which is why review failed on row 395; the
  row must land via the CoS stamp commit, not the worker's diff.
- The card's work is still uncommitted in the epic clone (`M capsule/unblocked.py` etc.). Nothing
  to do about that until the gate card lands; then reset the card and let the normal round run.

title: Capsule: mutation gate pushes implementers to reshape or delete tests (pure-addition heuristic, @skipIf hard flag)
body: Observed 2026-09-29/30 on t_1b26f70e (two rounds of test reshaping, then a real regression guard deleted to satisfy the gate; restored in review), t_f63e221f (comment revert to dodge the gate), t_d2b36dd4. The 'pure addition explains every revert failure' heuristic and the hard static flag on a new @skipIf (even a root-uid guard) push agents toward gate-shaped tests. Goal: gate reports these as info with a reason instead of a hard fail where a test is genuinely a guard, and the rule 'never delete a guard to satisfy the gate' is written into common-rules and the implementer contract. Needs a decision row (contract change).
why: Changes how the mutation gate treats tests and the implementer contract rule; says it needs a decision row (contract change).

title: C07b - Lander part 2: ff-only merge, push, and the revert rule
body:
Body: `lander.mode: land`: after C07a's checks pass, `git -C $CAPSULE_HOME/harness/main merge --ff-only
<commit>` into the release checkout (C08; never the dev checkout), then `git push origin main`; write the
marker json the keepers write today (`queue/capsule-corp/capsule/<branch>.json`: landed, landed_sha, suites,
deploy); `./deploy.sh --check`; drift -> an outbox `needs_input` line, never an apply. Red after push (CI or
a later red the suites did not catch): the lander never resets; the next pass pushes a revert commit (row
505) and opens a Korin incident. The lander holds one `caps.max_heavy` seat and runs at most one landing at
a time across boards (`guard_state` key `lander.busy`, compare-and-set). Intent examples extended: green ->
landed+pushed; push rejected (non-ff) -> re-check next pass, never force; red after push -> revert + incident.
Oracle 2: `tests/test_lander.sh` runs a real ff, a real refused ff and a revert on a temp bare remote.
Size: M. Deps: C07a, C08. Reviewer: Fable (pushes main; row 566 "data loss"). Owner's stamp is NOT needed
for the code; Q1 asks whether the lander may push main; `lander.mode` stays `dry-run` until he says so.

Amended 2026-10-18 (rows 598-600): Row 600 Q1: per-card push to origin/main for the capsule-corp harness repo; product boards land via one daily PR Owner merges; lander.mode dry-run until proven.
why: Lander part 2: edits the lander (a protected gate) and pushes main to origin, an effect outside the laptop (row 566 'data loss').

title: Other-app gauntlet: the bulk layer retains a whole image import per case (34 GB for 21 cases) and fills the disk; clean each case's import after scoring and cap sessions per run
body:
Incident 2026-09-28 13:58: night2-20260927 bulk layer (import_and_cull) wrote ~1.6 GB of session data per case into sessions/bulk; at 21/40 cases the 460 GB volume hit ENOSPC, breaking the Capsule keeper suites (W68) and a review. Owner approved deleting sessions/bulk, night1's sessions and the smoke runs (~75 GB freed). Fix in the gauntlet (other-app repo, tests/gauntlet + gauntlet/runner.py): (1) after a case is scored, delete its imported originals/copies and keep only the sample-renderer XMP/db, the scored outputs and previews (a per-layer retention policy, bulk = 'score only'); (2) a run-level cap: refuse to start a case when free disk < 20 GB, park the run with reason 'disk' (same shape as the usage parker); (3) a `gauntlet du --stamp` report by layer; (4) tests with a fake case that writes N MB and asserts retention + the disk guard (Z2: unit + one real tiny run). Then rerun night 2's bulk layer (--resume --layer bulk). Waits: release bar 6 (no other-app landing while a gauntlet runs) and the night-2 fail triage.

Amended 2026-09-29 00:05 (Owner: keep 30-40 GB always free): the disk guard threshold is 40 GB free, not 20: the runner refuses to start a case and parks the run with reason 'disk' below 40 GB free; per-case retention after scoring keeps only the sidecar/XMP, the verdict json, the log and one preview (no library copies, no imports, no full-size renders); target under 5 GB per full night. This card is a prerequisite for night 3 and for any bulk rerun.

Amended 2026-09-29 00:20 (Owner): the gauntlet's disk guard is 25 GB free (his hard limit for this use case), and an operator never launches a run under 30 GB free. Cleanup after the programme: sessions and previews of every run dir deleted, evidence archived to one tarball (pre-authorised).
why: Retention policy: deletes imported originals after scoring and caps disk; data deletion (Owner amended thresholds).

title: Dependency wait on an epic merging to main; tick releases it (inc_b862eccd)
body:
w377 note: ignore any mention below of report.v1 waits_on_epic or a tick._route 'wait' branch. Out of scope. capsule/tick.py is held at its size baseline: put the new logic in blocks.py or a new module and keep tick.py to a net-zero call line (a size raise under 20 lines needs CoS approval).

This card also closes inc_e45f9484 (t_8e245d81 is folded in).

Incident inc_b862eccd: CoS had to unblock t_71ac469b (and t_cfc438b5) by hand after epic/sample-app-screens-epic merged to main 36451c2 (human/done/114.json, 115.json, event 5923). The cards needed stats.py and /api/stats from that epic. tick.py:735 holds every left_undone report as needs_input. blocks.py promote_ready releases a dependency wait only through parent cards (db.py:333).

Write this test first. It must fail before the fix:
- capsule.tests.test_blocks.EpicMergeWait.test_wait_on_epic_releases_when_merged_to_main: use a temp git origin with main and epic/a. Put a card on epic/b into blocks.block(kind='dependency', waits_on='epic/a'). Assert the card stays todo/dependency while epic/a is not merged. Merge epic/a into main. Run blocks.release_merged_waits once. Assert the card is ready, waits_on_branch is NULL and one 'dependency_released' event names the main sha. Assert no outbox line asks a human to unblock.

Acceptance criteria:
1. db.py migration adds nullable tasks.waits_on_branch.
2. blocks.block accepts waits_on. It refuses a branch that is undeclared or is the card's own branch, and falls back to the needs_input hold in that case.
3. blocks.release_merged_waits(conn, cfg, repo) releases a waiting card when origin/<branch> is an ancestor of origin/main. A git error leaves the card waiting and never raises.
4. tick.py runs release_merged_waits each tick next to promote_ready (tick.py:1899).
5. (Removed in triage w377.) The report.v1 'waits_on_epic' field and the tick._route 'wait' branch are NOT in this card: contracts/schemas/report.v1.json is protected and needs Owner's approval, so it is a separate outside change. Workers reach the wait through the CoS `wait` verb only. Do not edit contracts/**.
6. Add the CoS verb `capsule human <board> <task> wait <epic-branch>` (human.py, interventions.py, __main__.py). Add 'wait' to incidents.ROUTINE_COS_KINDS, because it is a routine nudge.
7. Extra tests: test_wait_refuses_undeclared_branch, test_git_error_keeps_card_waiting, and (folded in from t_8e245d81, inc_e45f9484) capsule.tests.test_blocks.EpicMergeWait.test_wait_on_epic_releases_every_card_waiting_on_it: temp git repo with main and epic/x; two cards in todo/dependency with waits_on_branch=epic/x, one card waiting on unmerged epic/y; merge epic/x into main, call blocks.release_merged_waits once; both epic/x cards are ready, each with one dependency_released event carrying the main sha, the epic/y card stays todo. A second tick releases nothing and writes no duplicate event.

File set: capsule/db.py, capsule/blocks.py, capsule/tick.py, capsule/human.py, capsule/interventions.py, capsule/__main__.py, capsule/incidents.py, capsule/event_kinds.py, capsule/tests/test_blocks.py, capsule/tests/test_tick*.py.

The incident closes when the recurrence test passes on main.

## Incident inc_b862eccd (Korin post-mortem, row 456)
- Root cause: t_71ac469b needed stats.py and /api/stats. That code lived only on epic/sample-app-screens-epic, not on main. The card's hold could end only with a human unblock. The factory has no hold that waits for another epic to merge into main and releases itself. tick.py:782 (_route) sends every left_undone/issues report to "hold". tick.py:735 then calls blocks.block(kind="needs_input"), and only a human verb releases it. blocks.py:38-40 has a self-releasing "dependency" wait. But promote_ready (blocks.py:347-369) releases it only through task_links parents (db.py:333 open_parent). A parent card cannot express "branch X is merged to main". No caller passes kind="dependency", so workers never reach it. When the screens epic merged (36451c2), nothing re-checked the card. CoS released it by hand (human/done/114.json, event 5923). The same unblock text went to t_cfc438b5 (human/done/115.json), so two cards hit the same gap. Missing evidence: the board's own "blocked" event for t_71ac469b is outside my read set, so I cannot quote its reason text.
- Mitigation: Make the "dependency" wait able to wait on a declared epic branch merging into main, and release itself:
1. Add the nullable column tasks.waits_on_branch with a db.py migration.
2. Give blocks.block an optional waits_on=<branch> argument. It must be a declared epic other than the card's own. It sets waits_on_branch and routes the card to todo/dependency (blocks.py:38-40).
3. Add blocks.release_merged_waits(conn, cfg, repo). The tick runs it next to promote_ready (tick.py:1899). It moves a waiting card to ready when origin/<branch> is an ancestor of origin/main (git merge-base --is-ancestor). It writes a "dependency_released" event with the main sha.
4. Give the worker a way to name the wait: report.v1 gains an optional "waits_on_epic" field. This is a contract change, so Owner approves it on the card. tick._route returns "wait" when the field names a declared, unmerged epic. Any other value keeps today's needs_input hold.
5. Add the CoS verb `capsule human <board> <task> wait <epic-branch>` (human.py, interventions.py). It calls the same path, so CoS never has to unblock by hand again.
- Enforcer: capsule/blocks.py release_merged_waits, run every tick from tick.py next to promote_ready: it releases an epic-merge wait with no human verb. capsule/tests/test_blocks.py EpicMergeWait pins it, and the lander/CI unittest run blocks the merge when it fails.
- Recurrence test: `capsule.tests.test_blocks.EpicMergeWait.test_wait_on_epic_releases_when_merged_to_main` - write it first; it fails before the fix and passes after.
- [ ] `python3 -m unittest capsule.tests.test_blocks.EpicMergeWait.test_wait_on_epic_releases_when_merged_to_main` passes (the incident gate re-runs it on main).

# Audit capsule-corp and my-app Renovate coverage

Feature: INFRA-06. Size: about 2h. Protected: no. Suggested wave: 1.

## Goal and why

capsule-corp's config enables only the `github-actions` manager, yet the repo also pins compose images in `observability/docker-compose.yml` and Python tooling versions elsewhere. Row 139 says all four repos. Extend carefully without fighting deliberate pins, and cover my-app (no CI, board null, mounted read-only) only if it has a manifest.

## Scope

- Add the `docker-compose` manager for `observability/docker-compose.yml` with majors as PRs; explicitly exclude `docker/**` (images are pinned by `IMAGES.lock` and digest; Renovate must not rewrite them).
- Inspect `~/CodeBase/my-app` for any package manifest; if none, record 'no managers apply' in the PR and add no file.
- Write the decision in the PR body: which manager added and which pins deliberately left alone.

File set: .github/renovate.json

## Do not touch

`docker/**`, `docker/IMAGES.lock` (protected), `deps-allowlist.txt` semantics, workflows.

## Two oracles (Z2)

1. Fails before, passes after: A test (`tests/test_ci_yaml.sh` style or a small python check) asserting `docker-compose` is in `enabledManagers` and `docker/**` is in `ignorePaths`; fails before.
2. Independent check: `renovate-config-validator .github/renovate.json` exits 0; a Renovate dry run (`LOG_LEVEL=debug renovate --platform=local`) lists compose images and no `docker/**` file.

## Ordering

Depends on: none.

title: Detector: lane idle with ready work for 15 min (name the holder)
body:
On 2026-10-26 the capsule-corp lane sat idle for most of the day. Ready cards existed, but each time something held the epic clone: first a dirty clone from t_1c84a9be, then a card blocked on a false validator failure (t_56718d0c). `capsule unblocked` reported UNOWNED 0 throughout, and nothing alerted. The CoS only noticed when Owner asked why nothing was running.

Add a Z5 detector: when a board has 0 running and at least one ready card for 15 minutes or more, raise an event and an alert. The alert names the holder, the hold reason (clone-dirty or branch-busy plus the holding card and its block reason), and the oldest ready card. Surface it in `capsule status` ATTENTION and in `capsule unblocked`, so the CoS stop hook sees it.

Oracle: a fixture board with 0 running, a ready card, and a holder card blocked as needs_input for 16 minutes yields one idle-lane item naming the holder.
Second oracle: a board with a card running, or with no ready cards, yields none.


intake: rq_4a87fd4c; incident: none
why: New detector event and alert for an idle lane: ordinary observability code with two oracles.

title: Tick: sync an idle epic with main (epic_sync only runs after a gate pass)
body:
epic_sync runs only after_gate_pass, so an idle epic never picks up main. On 2026-10-24, W341 landed straight on main, the epic stayed behind, and card t_e5e5259a failed 5 runs on the stale base; the CoS merged main into the epic by hand (c200c286).
Add an idle-epic sync to the tick: when no card holds the epic clone and origin/main is not an ancestor of the clone HEAD, merge --no-ff and publish, with the same holds as after_gate_pass (dirty clone -> needs_input event, no merge).
Never sync while a card with a pinned start_sha is live on that epic.
Oracle: within one tick of main moving, the idle clone HEAD contains origin/main; a conflict gives an epic_sync_conflict event and no card is held. Z1 intent example required.

why: Idle-epic sync in the tick, reuses epic_sync holds: ordinary code, reversible.
